Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. Girish Chandra 
Lakhchaura, Advocate for the 
petitioner. 
Mr. Vipul Painuli, Brief Holder 
for the State. 
It is the case of the petitioner 
that the FIR is malafide and it has 
been filed to rage the vengeance by 
respondent no.3, Prakash Chandra, 
Sub-Inspector, In-charge Garjiya 
Police Post, Police Station Ramnagar, 
District Nainital because he wanted 
to book two rooms in the resort on 
the particular day, which could not 
be provided because the rooms were 
booked for the marriage party. 
Learned counsel for the 
petitioner had also argued that, in 
fact, earlier the respondent no.3 (“the 
informant”) has been taking rooms 
and other services from the resort,
free of costs. He has referred to 
Annexure No.7 that on one occasion, 
one guest named, Lalit Pandey of the 
informant has also stayed in the 
resort.
Let learned State counsel get 
instruction with regard to Annexure 
No.7.
List on 18.12.2023, just after 
fresh cases. 
(Ravindra Maithani, J.)

Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. G.S. Lakhchaura and Mr. 
Dushyant Mainali, Advocates for the 
petitioners.
Ms. Manisha Rana Singh, A.G.A. for 
the State.
It has been brought to the notice of 
the Court that another petition (CLCON 
No.346 of 2023) has been filed in the matter 
for Contempt of the Court against the 
Investigating Officer, as arrest has been 
made in defiance to the directions of the 
Hon’ble Supreme Court in the case of 
Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar and 
Another, (2014) 8 SCC 273.
Since both these matters arise from 
the same FIR, it would be appropriate that 
both are heard by one and the same 
Bench. 
Registry to seek directions for listing 
of both these cases before one and the 
same Bench. 
 (Ravindra Maithani J.) 
20.12.2023

WPCRL No.1655 of 2023
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. G.C. Lakhchaura, Advocate for 
the petitioners.
Mr. Pramod Tiwari, Brief Holder for 
the State.
The challenge in this petition is 
made to an FIR No. 512 of 2023, under 
Section 60 (1) (a) read with Section 21 of 
the Uttarakhand (U.P.) Excise Act, 1910
(“the Act”), Police Station Ramnagar, 
District Nainital.
According to the FIR, the police 
visited a resort and found that liquor was 
being served there. A case has been 
lodged as the liquor was served without 
any license.
Learned counsel for the petitioners 
would submit that the FIR is malafide; It 
has been filed to wreak the vengeance by 
the respondent no.3, Prakash Chandra 
Pokhriyal, Sub Inspector, In-Charge, 
Garjiya Police Post, Police Station 
Ramnagar, District Nainital because he 
wanted two rooms in the resort on a 
particular day. The room could not be 
provided because the rooms had already 
been booked for a marriage party. It is 
also argued that, in fact, a contempt 
petition was filed against the respondent 
no.3, the informant for making illegal 
arrest which is CLCON No. 346 of 2023, 
pending in this Court.
Learned counsel for the petitioner 
would submit that offence under Section 
60 of the Act, is not made out in the 
instant case. Having considered, this Court is of 
the view that this matter requires 
deliberation.
Issue notice to the respondent no.3.
Counter affidavit may be filed within 
three weeks. Two weeks thereafter, 
rejoinder affidavit, if any, may be filed.
List this matter on 26.02.2024.
Heard on Stay Application No. 1 of 
2023.
It is argued that the petitioner no.1 
has been arrested and granted bail.
Having considered, as an interim 
measure, till the next date of listing, 
further proceedings in terms of 
investigation etc, pursuant to FIR No. 512 
of 2023, under Section 60 (1) (a) read 
with Section 21 of the Act, Police Station 
Ramnagar, District Nainital shall remain 
stayed qua the petitioner no.2.
Stay application stands disposed of 
accordingly.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 27.12.2023 Jitendra

Rajeev Kumar Sah and another …..Petitioners
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and others …..Respondents
With
CLCON No. 346 of 2023
Rajeev Kumar and another …..Petitioners
Vs.
Arun Kumar Saini and others …..Respondents
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. G. C. Lakhchaura, Advocate and Mr. 
Dushyant Mainali, Advocate through video 
conferencing for the petitioners.
Ms. Manisha Rana Singh, D.A.G. for the 
State in WPCRL No. 1655 of 2023
Mr. Vipul Sharma, Advocate for the 
respondent no.2 in CLCON No. 346 of 2023
Mr. Lalit Sharma, Advocate for the 
respondent no. 3 in CLCON No. 346 of 2023.
Mr. Devesh Ghildiyal, Standing Counsel 
for the State in CLCON No. 346 of 2023.
Supplementary affidavits and counter 
affidavits are taken on record. IA No. 1 of 2023, 
IA No. 2 of 2024, IA No. 3 of 2024 and IA No. 4 
of 2024 stand disposed of accordingly.
In this petition, there are multiple 
allegations against the police officers with 
regard to manipulation of the records, 
malafide, forgery, illegal arrest etc. One of the 
allegations is that when illegally the resort was 
raided by the police officers, they took the DVR 
out and did not return it.
Now a supplementary affidavit dated 
02.03.2025 has been filed by the petitioners 
enclosing conversation between the Asif Khan, 
the Investigating Officer (“the IO”) with Hariom 
Sharma, who, it is stated is father of the 
petitioner no.2, which records that, in fact, on 
the date of conversation, the DVR was in the  custody of the IO, Asif Khan.
Let IO, Asif Khan file a short affidavit 
stating as to where is that DVR? How he get 
custody of it? What was the occasion for him to 
speak to Hariom Sharma on 13.12.2013? Has 
the DVR been sent for forensic examination? If 
yes, when?
This affidavit shall be filed within a week.
List on 17.07.2026 after fresh cases.
This Court requests learned State counsel 
to ensure that this order is communicated to 
the IO, Asif Khan and he files his affidavit 
within time.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.) 
 10.07.2026
Jitendra
